source.citation: Kushch, Volodymyr I. (2013). Micromechanics of Composites: Multipole Expansion Approach. Elsevier. ISBN 9780124076839.
source.location: Tables 3.1 to 3.3 (p. 67); Appendix A, sections A.1 to A.4 and Table A.1 (p. 465)

transcription.from: the published book (PDF), read on the page text
transcription.note: Conductivities are divided by that of the matrix, the contrast being the conductivity of the spheres over that of the matrix. The values of the appendix are the printouts the sample codes give as correct.

fcm_conductivity.description: Effective conductivity, over that of the matrix, of the finite cluster of 27 equal spheres on a 3x3x3 simple cubic block, volume fraction 0.2, contrast 10, closed by the modified Maxwell method (Eq. 2.65).

fcm_volume_fraction.description: Volume fraction of the spheres in the two finite-cluster test problems; the period of the block is (4 pi / (3 c))^(1/3) radii.

fcm_conductivity_contrast.description: Conductivity of the spheres over that of the matrix in the conduction test problem.

periodic_conductivity_sc.description: Effective conductivity, over that of the matrix, of the simple cubic array at the volume fraction 0.5 and the contrast 1e8 (Eq. 3.51).

fcm_bulk_modulus.description: Effective bulk modulus over that of the matrix for the finite cluster of 27 spheres, volume fraction 0.2, shear moduli ratio 1e6, Poisson ratios 0.3 (Eq. 4.123).

fcm_shear_modulus_1.description: Effective shear modulus (C1111 - C1122)/2 over the shear modulus of the matrix, same problem (Eq. 4.124).

fcm_shear_modulus_2.description: Effective shear modulus C1212 over the shear modulus of the matrix, same problem (Eq. 4.125).

fcm_shear_contrast.description: Shear modulus of the spheres over that of the matrix in the elasticity test problem.

fcm_poisson_ratio.description: Poisson ratio of the matrix and of the spheres in the elasticity test problem.

ruc_c1133.description: C1133/(2 mu0) of the simple cubic array, as printed by the sample code of the periodic elasticity problem.

notes: The printed column header of the infinite contrast is the symbol of infinity.
Tables 3.1 to 3.3 are complete; Table A.1 goes to the degree 50 in the book, of which the degrees 2 to 8 are transcribed.
Table conductivity_sc: Table 3.1, p. 67. Effective conductivity of the simple cubic array of spheres, over that of the matrix.
Table conductivity_bcc: Table 3.2, p. 67. Effective conductivity of the body-centered cubic array of spheres, over that of the matrix.
Table conductivity_fcc: Table 3.3, p. 67. Effective conductivity of the face-centered cubic array of spheres, over that of the matrix.

Table lattice_sums_sc: Table A.1, p. 465. First rows of the lattice sums of the simple cubic lattice of unit period, divided by N_ts = sqrt((t-s)!(t+s)!): harmonic Y_ts(0) and biharmonic Z_ts(0). The harmonic sum of degree 2, conditionally convergent, is given in the convention of the book.
In the conductivity tables the columns contrast_0 to contrast_infinity are the conductivity of the spheres over that of the matrix; contrast_infinity stands for perfectly conducting spheres.
